brief_title: Comparing the Extent to Which Maridebart Cafraglutide (AMG 133) is Made Available in the Body When Administered Using Two Subcutaneous Presentations After Multiple Doses
official_title: A Phase 1, Open-label, Randomized, Parallel Group, Multiple Dose Study to Assess the Relative Bioavailability of Maridebart Cafraglutide (AMG 133) as Two Subcutaneous Presentations in Participants Living With Overweight or Obesity

primary_outcomes.measure: Area Under the Plasma Concentration-time Curve from Time 0 to 28 days post dose (AUC 0-28) of Maridebart Cafraglutide
Maximum Observed Plasma Concentration (Cmax) of Maridebart Cafraglutide

brief_summary: The main objective of this study is to compare the pharmacokinetics of maridebart cafraglutide administered as a single dose using two different subcutaneous (SC) presentations in participants with overweight or obesity after they have received escalating doses of the study drug.

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults 18 to 60 years of age.
* Body mass index (BMI) between 25 and 35 kilograms per square meter (kg/m\^2), inclusive.
* Stable body weight, with less than 5 kilograms (kg) (11 pounds) of weight change in the past 3 months.
* No significant changes in diet or eating habits in the past 3 months.
* Generally healthy. People with certain well-controlled medical conditions, such as sleep apnea, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or underactive thyroid, may qualify if their treatment has been stable for at least 3 months and is approved by the study doctor.
* Willing to follow the study's birth control requirements, if applicable, during the study and for the study-defined period after the last dose of study drug.
* Able and willing to provide informed consent before participating in study procedures.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of diabetes or current diabetes, except diabetes during pregnancy, or blood sugar levels that meet the study's definition of diabetes.
* Certain hormonal conditions that can cause weight gain, such as Cushing's syndrome.
* History of pancreatitis (inflammation of the pancreas) or certain abnormal pancreatic blood test results.
* History of cancer within the past 5 years, except certain early-stage cancers or nonmelanoma skin cancers.
* Personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (MEN2).
* Uncontrolled thyroid disease or certain abnormal thyroid blood test results.
* Significant stomach or intestinal conditions, including delayed stomach emptying, ulcers, or inflammatory bowel disease, or a history of certain digestive system surgeries.
* Weight-loss surgery within the past 6 months.
* Significant heart disease, abnormal heart rhythms, or blood pressure or heart rate outside the study's allowed limits.
* Significant kidney or liver problems, or certain abnormal kidney or liver blood test results.
* Positive tests for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B, or hepatitis C, with certain exceptions for past hepatitis B vaccination or infection.
* History of certain serious or unstable mental health conditions, self-injury within the past 5 years, or any previous suicide attempt.
* History of ischemic optic neuropathy, a condition involving damage to the optic nerve caused by reduced blood flow.
* Allergy or intolerance to maridebart cafraglutide (AMG 133), similar medications, or their ingredients.
* Use of certain medications, including weight-loss or diabetes medications that act on glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) or glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), within the restricted time periods before the study.
* Use of certain herbal products, vitamins, or supplements within 30 days before enrollment, unless approved by the study doctor.
* Recent participation in another investigational drug study or previous participation in a study of maridebart cafraglutide.
* History of alcohol or drug abuse, recent illegal drug use, or positive alcohol or drug screening results not explained by permitted prescription medications.
* Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to breastfeed during the study or within the study-defined period after the last dose of study drug.
* Recent blood, plasma, or platelet donation within the study's restricted time periods.
* Recent strenuous exercise or unwillingness to follow study restrictions on physical activity, alcohol, recreational drugs, diet, or other activities.
* Difficulty providing blood samples because of poor vein access.
* Any other medical condition, abnormal test result, or circumstance that the study doctor believes could make participation unsafe or interfere with study procedures.
